claims.text: Replacing a small fraction of zirconium with silicon can form a (Zr1–xSix)B2 solid solution.
Reactive spark plasma sintering under a reducing atmosphere can produce the proposed material at 1600–1650 °C.
The resulting silicon-doped material will remain single phase.
Silicon substitution will enhance the sintering of ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature formulations.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have better liquid-metal corrosion resistance than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature formulations.
Silicon substitution produces lattice distortions in the homogeneous solid solution.
Silicon-induced lattice distortions enhance densification.
High-temperature exposure causes formation of a thin, silica-enriched passivating surface layer.
Silicon substitution enhances mass transport during sintering.
Enhanced mass transport enables densification at lower temperatures.
Silicon-related lattice modifications promote segregation of SiO2/B2O3-rich oxide phases at the surface during service.
The silicon-rich surface oxide phases improve oxidation resistance.
The silicon-rich surface oxide phases improve resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
The silicon-doped ZrB2 will achieve full densification at approximately 1600–1650 °C.
The silicon-doped ZrB2 will have mechanical strength equal to or greater than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Prior lower-temperature-processed specimens were typically prepared above 1700 °C and had inadequate oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Excessive silicon can cause phase segregation or nonuniform silicon distribution.
Performance may deteriorate above the stability range of the passivating layer.
